links.title: Harai-goshi-gaeshi on the IJF technique reference

about.en: The counter to Harai-goshi: as uke turns in and sweeps, tori hooks the leg uke is standing on, round the lower leg from behind, and reaps it. Recognised by the Kodokan as a technique in its own right.

en: Hips back and low the moment they turn in
Their supporting leg is the target, not the sweeping one
Hook it from behind and reap it
Your partner turns in for Harai-goshi, their right leg swinging back to sweep your thigh.
Drop your hips away and bend your knees so the sweep cannot lift you.
Hook your left leg round their lower left leg from behind, the leg they are standing on.
Reap that leg while their right leg is still sweeping, so neither foot is under them.
They fall onto their back beside you.

receiving.en: Your sweeping leg is still in the air when your standing leg is hooked from behind and reaped, which is the moment the throw becomes theirs. You land on your back or side with nothing underneath you. Chin tucked, slap wide with the free arm, and trust the grip you still hold to steady the landing.

viNotes.en: The sweep reaches you as a leg swinging back along the outside of your thigh, and that contact is the signal to drop your hips. Their other leg is then the only one on the mat. Find it by keeping your leg in contact with theirs rather than reaching for where you think it is, and hook it from behind the moment your legs meet.

cue.en: The sweeping hip throw is caught mid-turn: the leg its maker stands on is hooked from behind and reaped.
